headline: Day two after the blue sweep turned the AI rotation into capitulation: SOX -12/13%, memory and AI-power liquidated, retail and systematics dumping, and only APP, NET and the hyperscalers' existing capacity drawing buyers.
market_read: 5 Nov was the second-worst SOX day on record; desks describe forced de-grossing rather than a fundamental verdict. Jefferies' ADR desk (6 Nov) counts nine straight sessions of TMT net selling by both LOs and HFs, and Vanda (6 Nov, forwarded internally) saw systematics cut $74bn and retail sell single stocks at the fastest pace since 2020. The 4 Nov hyperscaler bid (UBS PB: 100% long buying) did not survive day two, though AMZN held up best; memory (MU, SNDK, Hynix) went from crowded long to the leading unwind. GS (Armbrust, 6 Nov) leans '1998 not 2000' and the 6 Nov pre-market bounce is led by the AI complex (LRCX buyback, MU, CRDO), but UBS (Cheong via Dwyer, 5 Nov) and Fubon (6 Nov) both say the low may not be in yet.

up.why: JPM's Schilsky (5 Nov) says bears went quiet and bulls were louder than in six months after the print; Jefferies (6 Nov) had APP as the best S&P 500 stock (+31%) yet still -47% YTD, and JPM's global specialists carry it as their TMT long. The move came in the worst tape of the year, which is the tell. APP is not in the Bloomberg-X mover or analog panels, so there is no attention or band reading to lean on. 1-5 days: likely to keep being a source of funds if de-grossing resumes Monday; 2-4 weeks: the short-covering-to-long-buying transition is the trade to watch.
up.confirm: Holds gains through another de-grossing session; PB data show long buying, not just covering.
up.weaken: Gives back the move as a source of funds; UBS's long META / short APP pair unwind fades and META outperforms.

up.why: UBS's Dwyer (5 Nov) calls AMZN one of the most consensus longs after UBS PB hyperscaler buying ran 100% long; Barclays' Rand (5 Nov) ties its leadership to having the most third-party compute. But UBS retail sold AMZN (-$52m) on 5 Nov. Its Bloomberg HOT score is 64.2 (60-<80 band), where AMZN's own history gives a 5-session median of -1.1% and a 10-session median of -2.9% (only 14% up, n=7); BULL 42.1. 1-5 days: crowding risk if the hyperscaler hide-out gets sold; 2-4 weeks: the existing-capacity scarcity story can hold if the 2028 build debate stays unresolved.
up.confirm: Keeps outperforming the SOX on down days; PB shows continued long buying.
up.weaken: Hyperscalers get sold for funding on the next liquidation leg; retail outflows keep naming AMZN.

up.why: LRCX announced a $25bn buyback (~11% of market cap) and led the 6 Nov pre-market bounce (+11.4%, Jefferies); BofA sales (6 Nov) relays Arya naming buybacks as a confidence restorer and LRCX in the baseline best-of-breed list. Bloomberg-X attention has fallen (z -1.42, Δz -2.12) with a HOT score of 33.5 (20-<40 band) and BULL 53.1, a neglected setup; the BULL-band analog gives a 5-session median of +2.4% (n=39). 1-5 days: high beta to any SOX relief; 2-4 weeks: needs WFE estimate stability.
up.confirm: Bounce holds after Monday's open; semicap names lead on up days.
up.weaken: SOX makes new lows despite the buyback; WFE estimates get cut on 2028 DC delays.

up.why: SemiAnalysis (5 Nov) argues Ironwood TPUs are now a viable alternative to CUDA for inference, with Oracle, OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta as customers; Barclays (5 Nov) notes GOOGL is capacity-constrained, which tempers its share of the hyperscaler bid. GOOG is not in today's Bloomberg-X or analog panels. This is an independent author's thesis, not desk flow, so it is a narrative to watch over 2-4 weeks rather than a positioning signal.
up.confirm: Desks start citing TPU share in GOOG/NVDA feedback; more external TPU deals.
up.weaken: Inference share data show no TPU gain; GOOG trades with the AI complex rather than the hyperscaler hide-out.

down.why: The crowded long-DRAM trade is the centre of the unwind: Jefferies' ADR desk (6 Nov) calls out the long DRAM / short China ADR pair unwinding with MU -15.5%, SNDK -22% and Hynix ADR -13.4%; BofA's Villani (6 Nov) puts the memory factor at -4.2σ and UBS PB (5 Nov) has memory net sold since May. MU is not in today's Bloomberg-X panel; its proxy SKHYNIX has falling attention (Δz -2.18) from a HOT 70.1 (60-<80) / BULL 80.6 (80-100) reading. This is crowding coming out, not a weaker fundamental story: BofA's Arya keeps MU in the base and bull cases. 1-5 days: high beta both ways (+8.2% pre-market 6 Nov); 2-4 weeks: depends on whether the pair unwind is complete.
down.confirm: Memory keeps underperforming on SOX bounces; more desks report DRAM longs being cut.
down.weaken: Memory leads the rebound with spot pricing intact; the MU buyback (from 9 Dec) draws real-money buyers.

down.why: JPM's Meyers (5 Nov) saw a relief rally then selling of anything touching DC picks and shovels, VRT -12.9%; BofA's Villani (6 Nov) puts Electric Grid Enablers at -7.7σ vs the S&P. Bloomberg-X attention is falling (Δz -2.37) while the HOT score is still 79.0 (60-<80) and BULL 76.5 (60-<80), so sentiment is still high relative to price. The analogs in those bands are thin (n=4-5) and say little. 1-5 days: vulnerable to further de-grossing; 2-4 weeks: hinges on the Texas DC rules and the '28 GW debate.
down.confirm: AI-power baskets keep lagging on bounce days; Texas pauses new DC approvals.
down.weaken: Hinojosa's 'laws, not bans' line is read as permitting continuing; power names lead a rebound.

down.why: JPM's See (6 Nov) has neoclouds -14% in the 5 Nov rout and CRWV fell ~10% (Jefferies). Two voices push back: CRWV's CEO says backlog is unaffected (via Jefferies, 5 Nov) and BofA credit (Goshko via Fenske, 5 Nov) calls debt-access fears overblown. Bloomberg-X tone is negative (-0.147) with attention below normal (z -1.28); HOT 39.9 / BULL 40.2, and the BULL-band analog has a 5-session median of -8.6% (n=16). 1-5 days: highest beta to funding headlines; 2-4 weeks: watch the SPCX $40bn GPU-financing syndication (Jefferies, 5 Nov) as a read on GPU credit appetite.
down.confirm: Bonds and CDS widen along with the equity; more neocloud financing pulled.
down.weaken: The credit holds while the equity bounces; contracted capacity comes online on schedule.

down.why: Fubon (via Jefferies' O'Mara, 6 Nov) says Taiwan margin debt is only ~12% off highs vs a 21.7% flush in July, so retail leverage is still unwinding (TSMC futures -9.8%); an Asian hedge-fund CIO tells O'Mara Taiwan retail is missing the top-down DC/power gap. Jefferies' expert relay (6 Nov) says TSMC already plans on ~70% of demand, which supports fundamentals. Bloomberg-X tone is flat (0.01) with attention below normal (z -1.15) and r7 -18.6%. 1-5 days: retail-margin selling can continue; 2-4 weeks: Fubon's bottom checklist (TSMC leads, fewer limit-downs, margin flush, TWD, SOX) is the guide.
down.confirm: Margin balances keep falling toward the July-style ~20% flush; TWD weakens.
down.weaken: TSMC leads the Taiwan rebound and limit-downs dry up.

down.why: Bernstein's spec sales (5 Nov) flags a gross-margin miss and a smartphone overhang into 2027, relaying research that multiples stay depressed; Jefferies had it -10% pre-market. Bloomberg-X attention is rising (Δz +1.80) with flat tone (0.003), so the attention is not bullish. HOT 41.6 (40-<60): the analog 5-session median is -2.2% (n=34). The prior ledger had shorts building into the print (Barclays, 4 Nov). 1-5 days: no catalyst to reverse; 2-4 weeks: the DC story needs FY27 numbers.
down.confirm: Estimate cuts follow; the stock lags on SOX bounce days.
down.weaken: Shorts cover on the AI-complex bounce; DC customer news.

themes.title: Capitulation or more to come? Desks disagree on who sold and whether the low is in
themes.text: Jefferies (Massey, 6 Nov) says LOs outsold HFs 55/45 on 5 Nov and TMT has seen nine straight days of LO and HF selling; TMTB (5 Nov) notes GS's desk instead saw LOs 'frozen out'. BofA's Villani (6 Nov) saw flows flip to net buying late in the day (retail's largest ETF buy day on record) while LOs and HFs kept selling semis and industrials. UBS (Cheong via Dwyer, 5 Nov) expects $100bn+ of risk-control selling and a possible Monday washout; Vanda (6 Nov) says retail capitulations usually come near bottoms but a few more days of pain are possible. GS (Armbrust, 6 Nov) leans '1998 liquidity event, not 2000'. All of these are flow and desk opinions, not forecasts.

themes.title: 2027 builds look intact; 2028 GW is what is being repriced
themes.text: JPM's Meyers (5 Nov), citing SemiAnalysis, says 50+ GW being built in 2027 should be mostly on track but 62+ GW of 2028 capacity is in question; GS's Callahan (5 Nov) says the market is trying to price 2028+ and SOX multiples have compressed ~50% from June/July. UBS's Dwyer (5 Nov) hears both 'pull-forward / 2027 peak' and 'cycle extended' readings. The GW figures are as the sources state them, without a facility vs IT-load basis, so they are not reconciled to the wiki's canonical GW framing. META's President (via Jefferies) says new US sites will be harder.

themes.title: Semis valuation floor: numbers up, multiples down
themes.text: Barclays' Rand (6 Nov): CY28 semi EPS is up ~24% since the late-June peak while multiples are down 19.5 turns, to ~13x CY28, with few long-term investors stepping in yet. BofA sales relaying Arya (6 Nov): SOX -37% from peak vs a 32% average drawdown, 13.7x forward, at most ~12% further downside to a ~12x trough; a 20% CY27 capex cut would mean a 35-40%+ EPS headwind for AI semis. Both say EPS cuts, not only cheap multiples, may be needed. Buybacks (LRCX $25bn, MU from 9 Dec) are the near-term support.

themes.title: SemiAnalysis: TPU is a credible inference alternative to CUDA
themes.text: SemiAnalysis (5 Nov, independent author, not a broker) says Google's Ironwood TPU now stakes a claim on inference, its external-TPU call has been proven with Oracle, OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta as customers, and NVIDIA is responding under pressure. This is a narrative input for GOOG vs NVDA rather than positioning evidence; no desk in today's mail relayed it.
